correctness.rationale: For each weak composition \(\mathbf r\) of \(n\), count ordered direct sums by \(\mathrm{GL}_n(q)\) stabilizers, count independent nilpotent diagonal blocks using the established formula \(q^{d^2-d}\), and divide by \(q^{n^2-n}\). This proves \(Q_n/\prod_iQ_{r_i}\), including zero components. Uniform \(Q_m-Q_\infty=O_q(q^{-m})\) gives the \(O_{q,k}(n^{k-2})\) expectation error and a uniform-composition total-variation error \(O_{q,k}(1/n)\), hence Dirichlet weak convergence. Cyclic nilpotents form an orbit with invertible centralizer size \((q-1)q^{n-1}\), yielding probability \(\prod_{i=2}^n(1-q^{-i})>1/2\); they and only they have exactly \(k\) splittings. Exhaustive verifier independently enumerates \((n,q)=(1,2),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2)\). Finite tests corroborate small instances but the limits rely on the proof.

originality.rationale: The final claim combines an exact all-arity expected invariant-splitting profile with a Dirichlet dimension-vector limit under uniform compatible-pair sampling and a strict >1/2 indecomposable-matrix majority whose median remains k. Searches of published research records, this ledger, and relevant centralizer/nilpotent-matrix literature disclosed no statement subsuming this combined ensemble law. The Gaussian multinomial factors and Fine–Herstein matrix count are classical, explicitly credited. Novelty is best-knowledge only, not independently certified.
residual_risks: Classical Hall algebra/q-binomial generating functions could encode the entire exact expectation and its Dirichlet limit under different terminology.
Finite-field random nilpotent-module literature not found by targeted searches may already state a size-biased splitting limit; priority is not certified.

The exact mean follows readily from the Fine–Herstein count, so the novelty assessment relies on the combined all-k distributional and median result, not on a claim of new Gaussian coefficient identities.

value.rationale: The count of invariant direct-sum decompositions is a natural invariant of the module (F_q^n,N), equivalently the idempotent centralizer profile. The theorem resolves its annealed all-arity dimension distribution and exhibits a mathematically substantive selection-bias phenomenon: a strict majority of individual nilpotents are indecomposable with L_k=k, while the mean grows polynomially and a uniformly chosen compatible pair has Dirichlet-distributed macroscopic block sizes. This contrast matters in random-module and centralizer statistics; it is not merely a renaming of a finite count. It makes no claim to a downstream application or unproved universality.
